children: Canada's main stock index closed in the red on Wednesday, as weaker metal prices weighed on miners, while hot US inflation data increased odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike later this month.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index
closed down 1.11%, at 35,584.46, falling from a three-week peak.
US consumer prices accelerated in September on higher gasoline costs, boosting expectations for a rate hike later this month.
Increased bets that the Fed will hike rates further to tame inflation also weighed on US indexes.
In Canada, the materials sector
was the biggest drag on the index, declining 4.3% as precious metal prices fell further after the data.
The rate-sensitive financial sector (.SPTTFS), which includes heavyweight banks, also fell 0.5%. Technology shares
fell 2.4% with Celestica
down 9.2% and Shopify
falling 2.2% .

"Canada will join other global central banks in hiking interest rates, but I don't think they're going to deliver as much as futures or the bond market is currently expecting," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones
The energy sector
gained just 0.07%, as oil prices held firm over $100 per barrel
Reuters reported that Iran was using new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections
Yields on the Canadian benchmark 10-year bond (CA10YT=RR) rose to 3.872%.
Canada is pursuing a trade pact with India and closer EU ties to reduce reliance on the US, ahead of Indian PM Narendra Modi's visit in December
Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings
will buy a majority stake in India's IDBI Bank
in a deal worth 528.78 billion Indian rupees ($5.56 billion), the Indian government said. Fairfax shares were flat.
